headline: Banks, MFSs told to suspend payment services for illegal loan apps
summary: Bangladesh Bank has ordered a crackdown on unauthorized lending apps that harass borrowers with high interest rates and data theft.
details: Bangladesh Bank has instructed banks, mobile financial service (MFS) providers, and payment service providers (PSPs) to immediately stop providing payment services to operators of unauthorized online lending apps.
The central bank also requested the BTRC to remove these illegal apps from platforms like the Google Play Store to permanently stop their operations.
These apps often charge exorbitant interest rates and gain unauthorized access to users' contacts, photos, videos, and text messages without their knowledge.
Borrowers who fail to repay may face blackmail and threats to publish sensitive personal information and photographs on social media.
Citing the Payment and Settlement Systems Act 2024, Bangladesh Bank stated that operating a lending platform without its approval is a punishable offense.
The Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit (BFIU) has already identified 30 illegal apps, including Sathi Loan, Pop Cash, and Quick Taka, involved in extortion and fraud.
Banks and MFS providers facilitating transactions for these apps could also be considered involved in the offense as financial transaction channels.
caption:
Beware of quick digital loans! Bangladesh Bank has ordered a total shutdown of payment services for illegal lending apps.

Bangladesh Bank has instructed banks, mobile financial service (MFS) providers, and payment service providers (PSPs) to immediately stop providing payment services to operators of unauthorized online lending apps.

The central bank also requested the BTRC to remove these illegal apps from platforms like the Google Play Store to permanently stop their operations.

These apps often charge exorbitant interest rates and gain unauthorized access to users' contacts, photos, videos, and text messages without their knowledge.

Borrowers who fail to repay may face blackmail and threats to publish sensitive personal information and photographs on social media.

Citing the Payment and Settlement Systems Act 2024, Bangladesh Bank stated that operating a lending platform without its approval is a punishable offense.

The Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit (BFIU) has already identified 30 illegal apps, including Sathi Loan, Pop Cash, and Quick Taka, involved in extortion and fraud.

Banks and MFS providers facilitating transactions for these apps could also be considered involved in the offense as financial transaction channels.

headline: 1,044 die as measles outbreak spreads across Bangladesh
summary: Eight more people died in 24 hours, bringing the total number of confirmed and suspected measles deaths to 1,044 this year.
details: Eight more patients died with measles-like symptoms in the last 24 hours, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
This brings the country's combined tally of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths to 1,044 for the year.
Of the total deaths, 944 are classified as suspected measles deaths, while 100 have been laboratory-confirmed.
In the same 24-hour period, 1,239 new suspected cases were reported, bringing the cumulative number of suspected cases nationwide to 175,198.
Additionally, 81 new confirmed measles cases were recorded, bringing the total number of laboratory-confirmed infections to 20,282.
Since March 15 this year, a total of 154,420 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalised across the country.
According to DGHS data, 148,465 of those hospitalised patients have recovered.
caption:
1,044 deaths and over 175,000 suspected cases. A measles outbreak is gripping Bangladesh.

Eight more patients died with measles-like symptoms in the last 24 hours, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

This brings the country's combined tally of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths to 1,044 for the year.

Of the total deaths, 944 are classified as suspected measles deaths, while 100 have been laboratory-confirmed.

In the same 24-hour period, 1,239 new suspected cases were reported, bringing the cumulative number of suspected cases nationwide to 175,198.

Additionally, 81 new confirmed measles cases were recorded, bringing the total number of laboratory-confirmed infections to 20,282.

Since March 15 this year, a total of 154,420 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalised across the country.

According to DGHS data, 148,465 of those hospitalised patients have recovered.
